# FishSET GUI Quickstart Guide

<div class="quickstart-hero">
FishSET is a set of statistical programming and data management tools for organizing fishery data,
creating model inputs, and evaluating policy scenarios.
This guide gives new users a fast path through the FishSET GUI.
</div>

## What the GUI does

The FishSET GUI helps you move from raw data to model-ready outputs without writing code.
The app saves data, plots, and logs to your project folder so you can return to the work later.

Use the GUI when you want to:

- load and organize data in a local FishSET project folder;
- check and clean data before analysis;
- create derived variables and model inputs;
- fit models and review cross-validation results;
- evaluate management scenarios and summarize policy impacts.

## Before you start

<div class="quickstart-note">
1. Run `library(FishSET)` and then `run_fishset_gui()`.
2. Choose a FishSET folder that will hold the project database, output files, and logs.
3. Have your main data ready; port, spatial, gridded, and auxiliary files are optional.
4. If you plan to use mapping or policy tabs, make sure the spatial file includes the zone information you need.
5. New users should start with the tabs in the order shown below.
</div>

## Quick path through the app

### 1. Upload Data

Open the **Upload Data** tab first.
Set your FishSET folder, create or select a project, and load the files you want to use.
The main data table is required.
If your workflow needs them, add port, spatial, gridded, or auxiliary data as well.

### 2. Select variables

Use **Select variables** to map the important columns used throughout the app.
This is where you identify IDs, dates, coordinates, and any other fields needed later.
If the data does not already contain a trip, haul, or zone ID, create one here.

### 3. QAQC and Explore the data

Use **QAQC** to check for missing values, duplicates, outliers, and spatial problems.
Use **Explore the data** to inspect tables and plots before moving on.
If you make corrections, save the updated data back to the FishSET database.

### 4. Format Data

The **Format Data** menu contains the tools used to build model inputs.
Use **Compute New Variables** to create derived fields such as CPUE, trip summaries, and spatial metrics.
Then use **Define alternative fishing choices** and **Create expected catch matrix** before running **Format Model data**.

### 5. Modeling

The **Modeling** menu is where the discrete choice model is built and evaluated.
Use **Model Design** to define the model structure, **Model Fit** to estimate the model,
and **Model Cross Validation** to check predictive performance.

### 6. Policy

The **Policy** menu is for scenario analysis.
Use **Zone Closure** to define closed or restricted areas.
Then run **Policy Simulations** and review **Summarize effort redistribution** and **Summarize welfare impacts**.

### 7. Bookmark Choices

**Bookmark Choices** is currently under development.
It will eventually store and reload actions taken in the GUI.

## What gets saved automatically

- Project data are stored in the local FishSET database.
- Plots and tables are written to the project output folder.
- Function calls and input values are written to the project log files.
- The report template in the project `doc` folder can be used to assemble a reproducible report.
